program_overview.title: Algorithmic Trading Masterclass
program_overview.tagline: The quant skill set, taught as engineering: Python for markets, strategies you can backtest honestly, risk management first, then machine learning, no profit promises, real capability.
program_overview.description:
Algorithmic trading is a serious quantitative discipline, and this course treats it as one, not as a get-rich pitch. It builds the strategy-and-research half of the field in order: Python for financial data, technical and statistical analysis, then strategy design and honest backtesting (including the traps, lookahead bias, overfitting, survivorship, that make bad strategies look brilliant), then risk management and position sizing taught before anything goes near live markets, and finally machine learning for trading, used with the scepticism the domain demands. Throughout, the message is consistent and repeated: markets carry real risk of loss, backtests do not predict the future, and this is education, not financial advice. A finale month builds a fully backtested strategy system and sits the final exam.

The pace is honest: ten teaching months at two live classes a week plus four to six hours of practice, with two more in hand. Problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams, and a final exam that decides the certificate with a free retest.

Backtesting honesty is a core theme: the biases that fake good results are named and defeated
Risk management before live markets, not as an afterthought
Machine learning applied with domain scepticism, not hype
Honest about risk on every page: education, not financial advice, no profit claims
Real assessment: weekly problem sets, monthly mixed reviews, phase exams and a final exam with a free retest

faqs.question: What does this algorithmic trading course cover?
faqs.answer: The research-and-strategy half of quant trading, taught as engineering: Python for financial data, technical and statistical analysis, strategy design across momentum, mean-reversion and volatility, honest backtesting that defeats lookahead, overfitting and survivorship bias, risk management and position sizing, then machine learning for trading with sentiment and alternative data. A finale month builds a fully backtested strategy system and sits the final exam. It is education, not financial advice.

faqs.question: How long does it take to learn algorithmic trading properly?
faqs.answer: Ten months of teaching at 2 live classes a week plus 4 to 6 hours of practice, with two more months in hand for learners who need them. The three teaching phases build the skill and its real-world application; the finale month ships a capstone and sits the final exam.

faqs.question: How am I assessed? Is the certificate just for attending?
faqs.answer: No. Problem sets follow every class with written feedback, monthly reviews deliberately mix new material with earlier topics, each phase ends with a cumulative exam, and the course ends with a final exam: a practical build plus written questions from the whole syllabus. Passing earns the certificate; falling short earns focused revision and a free retest.

faqs.question: Is this financial advice? Will I make guaranteed profits?
faqs.answer: No, and be wary of anyone who says otherwise. This is an engineering and quantitative course: it teaches you to research, build, backtest and automate trading systems, not what to buy or a way to get rich. Markets carry real risk of loss, backtest results do not guarantee future returns, and we make no profit claims of any kind. What you gain is genuine, in-demand skill; what you do with real money afterwards is your own decision and your own risk.

faqs.question: How is this different from your trading automation course?
faqs.answer: This course is the research-and-strategy half: what to trade, why, and how to know whether a strategy is real, statistics, backtesting honesty and machine learning. The trading automation course is the systems half: how to build reliable, production-grade bots that execute through broker APIs with monitoring and safeguards. Many serious learners take both; this one makes you the researcher, that one makes you the systems engineer.

faqs.question: Do I need finance or trading experience to start?
faqs.answer: No. Markets and the maths you need are taught from the ground up inside the course. What helps most is comfort with logical thinking and a willingness to be sceptical of your own results, which is the single most important habit in quantitative trading.
